cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: Company mail goes first; that is the rule. The Company mail today is one sack, one clerk, and a boat that could carry forty. Nine grain barges wait behind it.

left.label: Mail first, as written
left.outcome: One sack rises grandly through the chamber.

right.label: Mail waits for the grain
right.outcome: The clerk complains by wire. From your own telegraph office.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: Two vessels claim the same arrival bell. I have consulted the Compact. It provides that the Keeper decides, which I note is unhelpful, and that the Keeper's decision is final, which is worse.

left.label: The Aldmere boat
left.outcome: "Duly." The Sorrel bargee says something about Aldmere inspectors.

right.label: The Sorrel boat
right.outcome: "Duly." He writes it down a little harder than necessary.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! A Board member's private launch, brass and mahogany, is at the bottom of the queue. I need not say what a magnificent impression it would make to bring it up first.

left.label: Bring it up first
left.outcome: The launch gleams. The queue does not.

right.label: It takes its turn
right.outcome: "Its turn. Of course. A principled position, Keeper. A brave one."

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: My convoy is four boats and I would rather they went through together. Splitting an armed convoy is how accidents start. Your queue would rather they didn't.

left.label: Together
left.outcome: Four boats, one hour, nobody else moves.

right.label: One at a time, in turn
right.outcome: "Understood. It won't come to trouble." It does not.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A woman with a sick child asks to jump the queue for the physician on the Aldmere side. The child is quiet in the way children should not be. Eleven boats are ahead of her.

left.label: Bring her through now
left.outcome: Nobody in the queue complains. Not aloud.

right.label: Send for Stroud instead
right.outcome: Stroud comes to the boat. It takes an hour. The child lives.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A tug with six barges in tow wants the chamber six times in a row. The rule says arrival order. The tug says it has been doing this for twenty years.

left.label: Six in a row
left.outcome: An afternoon of one tug. The queue plays cards.

right.label: Alternate with the queue
right.outcome: The tug master spits. Twenty years, he says.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: The Sorrel escort vessel has moored across the approach to my inspection post. I note that this is not forbidden. I note also that it is not an accident.

left.label: Have it moved
left.outcome: Solas moves it himself, without comment.

right.label: Inspect from the towpath
right.outcome: "I can. I shall. I note it."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Board notes, Keeper, that the summit passed eleven fewer vessels than Lock 8 last month. Lock 8 is downhill. I would like an explanation I can send without wincing.

left.label: Fewer inspections this month
left.outcome: Numbers rise. Crane's eyebrows rise with them.

right.label: Lock 8 has more water
right.outcome: "Water. Yes. I shall not send that."

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: One of my men has been drinking at the Wheel and started something with a lock hand. My people, my discipline. Unless you would rather it was yours.

left.label: Your discipline
left.outcome: The man is sent down the west flight that night. Quietly.

right.label: The town's law
right.outcome: Ilse fines him. He pays. Solas watches.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: An Aldmere magistrate on a private boat produces a writ commanding the Keeper to give him precedence over 'commercial traffic'. The writ is not addressed to a Company lock.

left.label: Honor the writ
left.outcome: He passes. Crane looks pained; the writ is irregular and he knows it.

right.label: This is a Company gate
right.outcome: He threatens a report. Pell frames the report.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: The night watch reports a boat that moved up three places in the queue while the others slept. Its bargee says the others agreed. The others say otherwise.

left.label: Send it to the back
left.outcome: The queue cheers, briefly.

right.label: Where it is, it stays
right.outcome: The queue learns something about nights.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: An extraordinary situation. The Compact grants precedence to 'perishable foodstuffs'. The vessel before us carries ice. I have been unable to determine whether ice perishes.

left.label: Ice perishes
left.outcome: "A bold reading. I shall cite you."

right.label: Ice is a mineral
right.outcome: "Also bold. I shall cite you for that too."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: A Sorrel newspaperman has asked for a place on the first boat of the day, to see the sunrise from the summit. Think of the description, Keeper. Think of the adjectives.

left.label: Give Hesse the sunrise
left.outcome: The adjectives are many and mostly about Pell.

right.label: He can queue like anyone
right.outcome: The Courier describes the queue instead.

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: An Aldmere boat has been moored alongside my convoy all night, and a man on it has been counting my crates. I have not touched him. I am telling you before I have to decide whether to.

left.label: Move the Aldmere boat
left.outcome: The counter is Crane's clerk. Crane is unrepentant.

right.label: Counting is not a crime
right.outcome: "No. It's how they start."

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A funeral boat, black cloth over a long shape, asks quiet passage before the day's traffic. The Hullfolk at the tiller do not ask for a fee. They do not ask at all; they wait.

left.label: Open the gate in silence
left.outcome: The chamber fills without a bell. The queue takes off its caps.

right.label: The queue is the queue
right.outcome: They wait four hours. Nobody sings.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: Fog. Boats are arriving that cannot see the gate. The hands want to close until it lifts. The bargees want a lamp on the sill and a chance.

left.label: Close until it lifts
left.outcome: A wasted morning and no dented hulls.

right.label: Lamps on the sill; keep working
right.outcome: One barge kisses the gate. Nothing breaks. This time.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: I have prepared a revised order-of-passage schedule based on cargo class, arrival bell and shore of origin, weighted. It is eleven pages. I believe it would end all disputes.

left.label: Adopt it
left.outcome: Disputes end. Everyone hates the schedule equally, which is a kind of peace.

right.label: The Keeper decides, as written
right.outcome: "I anticipated that. Page eleven addresses it."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper, a Board member's nephew was made to wait behind a coal barge. Behind coal, Keeper. I have had a letter. I have had two.

left.label: Apologize by wire
left.outcome: You sign a letter you did not write.

right.label: Coal keeps Aldmere warm
right.outcome: "It does. Nephews do not know that."

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: Your lock hand, the Dray girl, has told my sergeant that convoys wait like anyone. My sergeant has told her what he thinks of that. She won. I thought you should know who runs your gate.

left.label: She does, at the paddles
left.outcome: "Good. I'd rather deal with someone who wins."

right.label: Remind her who decides
right.outcome: Mirren says nothing. She says it very clearly.

cards.speaker: src_stranger
cards.text: A Concordance pilgrim on foot asks to ride the next boat through, any boat, to reach the Lamp Vigil by dusk. No bargee wants a stranger aboard. One might, for a mark.

left.label: Pay the mark
left.outcome: She goes through on a coal barge, singing quietly.

right.label: She walks the towpath
right.outcome: She thanks you anyway. It is a long walk.
